title: SLI Health Commitments Timeline and Rollback Thresholds for Dedicated Deployments
creator: Riley Chen
description:
Objective: Create a tracked initiative that binds SLI health signals for Dedicated deployments to a deterministic timeline of actions (monitor -> throttle -> freeze -> rollback) and surface those actions in the Initiative Tracker so product, SRE, and sales can act quickly.

Why this matters: Dedicated customers require predictable behavior during regressions (e.g., kernel/quantization changes, autoscaler misconfig). Today we only surface error budget windows; this initiative creates an explicit commitments timeline and automation triggers so teams can respond consistently and customers see faster remediation.

Scope:
- Define SLI bundle for Dedicated (names and calculation windows):
  1) generate_p95_latency_ms (rolling 5m / 1h)
  2) request_success_rate (1 - 5xx_rate) (rolling 5m / 1h)
  3) token_completion_accuracy (synthetic prompt regression set) (daily)
- Map SLI deviations to concrete initiative actions over a time window ("SLI Health Commitments Timeline"). Example timeline below.

SLI Health Commitments Timeline (proposed):
- T+0 (detect): Alert to oncall when any SLI breaches soft threshold for 5m.
- T+15m (assess): If soft breach persists and error-budget burn-rate > 2x over 30m, mark initiative state = "At Risk" and notify PM + sales for impacted tenants.
- T+30m (throttle): If SLI still degraded and burn-rate > 3x, apply automated progressive throttle (canary scale down / limit concurrent requests for new sessions) and set initiative state = "Throttle Applied".
- T+60m (freeze rollout): If after throttle no improvement and burn-rate > 4x for 30m, freeze any rolling updates and pause scheduled Dedicated capacity changes; set initiative state = "Freeze".
- T+90m (rollback): If degradation continues and customer impact high OR token-accuracy regression detected on daily synthetic set, initiate automated rollback to previous verified model/kernel within dedicated pool and set initiative state = "Rollback Initiated".

Rollback safety rules:
- Rollback action only executed if at least two independent signals agree (latency + 5xx OR latency + synthetic regression).
- If rollback target differs by quantization/precision level, pick highest-compatibility candidate verified in QA window (link to candidate ledger in docs).
- Rollback should wait for confirmation of snapshot availability in storage (S3 snapshot ID present) to avoid partial state.

Acceptance criteria (PRD level):
- Initiative Tracker UI shows per-tenant initiative state (Normal / At Risk / Throttle Applied / Freeze / Rollback Initiated) and timestamped transitions.
- Automation hooks created: api endpoints for apply_throttle, freeze_rollout, execute_rollback with RBAC and audit logs.
- Alerting policy templates and runbook pages linked from initiative view.
- Monthly report shows number of automatic throttles/freezes/rollbacks and false-positive rate < 10% for throttle actions.

Telemetry and dashboards:
- Dashboard per Dedicated pool showing: p95 latency, 5xx rate, synthetic regression score, error budget remaining, burn rate (1h, 24h).
- Initiative timeline visualization and CSV export for audit.

Trade-offs and notes:
- Conservative thresholds reduce false positives but increase time to remediate; chosen thresholds are intentionally aggressive for Dedicated customers with SLA contracts.
- Progressive throttle chosen over immediate rollback to reduce blast radius for multi-tenant pools.
- Full automation requires engineering work on snapshot verification and RBAC for rollback endpoints (see dependencies).
